collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE I: SONGS, CHANTS, SPEECHES AND WELCOMES (LCA-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola sings, chants and speaks for itself: welcoming a new leader, wishing travelers luck, greeting newcomers and newborns, rallying for hard work, standing up for each other, and arguing about who gets the next verse.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A villager criticizes a popular decision at the gathering: hear them out, or ask them to accept the vote.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The village voted, almost everyone in favor, to build the new granary on the hill. (subject) voted against it, and has stood up at the gathering to say so again: the hill floods in the big rains, and the grain will rot. (friend) thinks the matter is settled and (subject) should accept the vote. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village listens. (subject) shows them the old flood marks on the rocks. Some people change their minds; many do not. They agree to build on the hill, but higher up, and to dig a ditch around it. (subject) is still not happy, but (subject.he/she) helps dig the ditch.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) asks (subject) to accept the vote, and the gathering agrees. The granary goes up on the hill. The next big rains come, and the floor of the granary is soaked. Nobody says anything to (subject). (subject) says nothing either. They move the grain together.
